sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-lessons-2026-10-08-r1/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: 'Quality Checks' row 3 (#2 instruction_preserves_natural_human_voice) and 'Internal Quality Checks' row 3 (same text; no extra annotation cells or drawing text for this row); 'Deterministic Checks' row 13 check-instruction-content.py ('Voice and grammar are left to the rubric'); read via zipfile in memory (openpyxl not installed in this Python)
evidence: STRENGTHS: instruction.md reads as a real recruiting lead talking: first person, contractions ("don't", "it's", "mustn't", "nobody's"), varied sentence length, reasons given ('Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled', line 1; 'dragging is welcome but optional', line 3; 'We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout', line 11; the 'check it yourself the way we'll use it' line 13). No marketing gloss: grep for seamless|robust|delve|leverage|ensure|comprehensive|intuitive over instruction.md and both notes returns nothing. No bullet lists in the brief. Lines 15-19 are a denser runtime-contract paragraph but stay conversational ('How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call', 'The browser side is free to pull fonts or a script from a CDN if that helps'). hireops_rules.md sections 1-7 and 9 keep the same team voice with reasons ('We like to know where a card was when it was rejected, because reopening takes it back...', line 50-51; 'We're usually in the middle of something when an update lands, so...', line 125; 'Candidates are outside the company, so...', line 197). The repeated idiom 'turned down' (9 occurrences) is consistent idiolect rather than robotic cadence. integration.md lines 1-14 are template-controlled impersonal runtime prose, which is expected. DEFECT: hireops_rules.md section 8 'Runtime file paths' (lines 202-208) is task-authored (it appears in no other project and not in the template) and switches abruptly from the team's first-person, reason-giving voice into an impersonal deployment spec addressed at the builder: 'The runtime may launch Node from a working directory other than the application directory. It runs as an unprivileged user and may launch a writable copy of the submitted application. Resolve bundled UI and seed files relative to the entry or module directory, never by assuming the current working directory is `/app`. Honor the supplied `DB_PATH` for persistent storage. The launch environment contains `PATH`, `HOME`, `NODE_PATH`, `PORT` and `DB_PATH`; do not rely on inherited shell variables.' No 'we/I', no user reason, imperative 'Resolve... Honor... do not rely', and it describes grader-harness launch behavior ('a writable copy of the submitted application'). The quality-checks reference lists 'a voice that changes between instruction.md and the notes' as a defect for this row, and Colderwater lesson 12 (portal flag) says to write notes in the requester's voice with reasons and never tell the builder how to build something just so the grader can test it. Minor related observations (not separate defects of this row): the same section spells 'Honor' while instruction.md line 15 says 'honour' (row 3 territory); integration.md lines 15-19 (symlink/NODE_PATH delivery paragraph) are task-added beyond the template but match the template file's impersonal register, so they do not change voice within that file. No runtime evidence is relevant to this row; raw-evidence-index.json exists (sha256 8df7cafe...51bc) but was not needed.
counterexample: A portal QC reviewer reading the notes cold moves from section 7 ('Candidates are outside the company, so nothing their browser receives may contain...') to section 8's 'Resolve bundled UI and seed files relative to the entry or module directory... Honor the supplied DB_PATH... do not rely on inherited shell variables.' and flags row 2 for a voice change (LLM/spec-sheet prose pasted into a human brief) and row 1 for build-recipe/grader-driven instructions, exactly the pattern Colderwater lesson 12 records as a portal flag. Builders are not graded differently by this, so the cost is a QC rejection, not a scoring error.
suggested_fix: Rewrite hireops_rules.md section 8 in the team's voice with a reason (e.g. 'Our servers don't always start Node from /app and run it as a locked-down user, sometimes on a copy of the folder, so find your pages and seed file relative to server.js and keep the database wherever DB_PATH says; don't count on any shell settings beyond PATH, HOME, NODE_PATH, PORT and DB_PATH.'), or move those facts into integration.md's runtime paragraph, and use one spelling of honour/honor.
